# Coastal pipeline review

**Meeting date:** Thursday, 30 Oct 2025  
**Meeting:** Coastal pipeline call  
**Attendees:** Bettina Kroll, Sofia Marchetti, Kwame Adjei-Rowe, June Osei-Lark

## Summary

The call focused on operational blockers affecting the Coastal pipeline. Discussion stayed with scheduling workflows, buyer follow-up and materials needed for the next conversations. No pricing decisions were made during the call.

Bettina asked that the next round of demonstrations use customer-specific arrival patterns rather than the standard sample yard. June will review the resulting proposal language for consistency with what Pemberline Dock actually supports.

## Account discussion

### Pellucid Harbor Logistics

- The dispatch team wants a clearer view of trucks arriving before their assigned windows. In the walkthrough, an early arrival at door 6 appeared beside an on-time appointment without enough visual distinction for the gate clerk.
- The next demonstration should include a Gulf Coast morning sequence: overnight arrivals, a shift handover and two trailers competing for the same unload window.
- Bettina will obtain a redacted dispatch sheet so the team can reproduce the sequence without using driver phone numbers.

### Driftmoor Marine Freight

- Kwame described a mismatch between the barge arrival board and the dock appointment view. The operations contact wants to hold a tentative unloading slot while the vessel arrival remains subject to change.
- Bettina asked, “Can we use Kwame's port account to test the tentative-slot walkthrough before the next coastal demo?”
- The group agreed to show the distinction between a provisional appointment and a committed door assignment, including what the afternoon dispatcher sees when the arrival moves.
- Kwame will send the current screen sequence and the specific point where dispatch loses track of the revised time.

### Saltmarsh Provisions

- Corinne Ashdown wants the receiving supervisor to see late inbound loads before allocating the next wave of grocery deliveries.
- The proposed demonstration will follow a chilled load arriving at door 3 during the early shift, with a delayed unload pushing the following appointment.
- Bettina will ask Corinne Ashdown whether the supervisor works primarily from the appointment board or an exported receiving report.

### Covey & Lark Retail

- The warehouse team requested a simpler explanation of how rescheduling affects the door view. The last walkthrough moved too quickly between the yard queue and appointment details.
- I will prepare a shorter sequence using one inbound home-goods trailer, one occupied door and a single reschedule.

## Action items

- **Bettina:** Collect the dispatch example and confirm the Saltmarsh Provisions demonstration workflow.
- **Kwame:** Send the revised-arrival screen sequence.
- **Sofia:** Rework the Covey & Lark Retail walkthrough.
- **June:** Review proposal wording after the demonstration outlines are circulated.
